In the randomized nivo/chemo arm (A1), 25 patients had baseline C1D1 CyTOF data with usable OS follow-up (14 deaths, 11 censored). Using censoring-aware Kaplan-Meier/log-rank analysis with median splits within this cohort, four baseline circulating T/NKT populations were associated with 1-year overall survival after BH correction across the seven tested T-cell populations.

Favorable associative biomarkers:
- Higher NKT cells (% of leukocytes): median cutoff 0.016406; high group KM 1-year OS 0.900 vs 0.364 in the low group; log-rank p=0.00494, q=0.0247; Cox HR high vs low=0.212 (95% CI 0.065-0.690).
- Higher Tbet+ T cells (% of CD3+ cells): median cutoff 0.179298; high group KM 1-year OS 0.808 vs 0.455 in the low group; log-rank p=0.0106, q=0.0247; Cox HR=0.239 (95% CI 0.073-0.782).
- Higher Tbet+ TCRgd+ T cells (% of TCRgd T cells): median cutoff 0.792079; high group KM 1-year OS 0.808 vs 0.455 in the low group; log-rank p=0.0250, q=0.0437; Cox HR=0.287 (95% CI 0.089-0.920).

Adverse associative biomarker:
- Higher Ki-67+ T cells (% of CD3+ cells): median cutoff 0.966289; high group KM 1-year OS 0.333 vs 1.000 in the low group; log-rank p=0.00998, q=0.0247; Cox HR=4.27 (95% CI 1.30-14.01).

HLA-DR+ T cells, HLA-DR+ non-naive CD4 T cells, and HLA-DR+ non-naive CD8 T cells were not significant after FDR correction. These findings are associative and hypothesis-generating because the baseline nivo/chemo CyTOF subset was small and the models were unadjusted.
